The core mechanism involves identifying objects within a sequence of images and storing their features for later analysis. This process enables temporal inference of object properties such as movement or action. The system operates under the assumption that features remain consistent across frames, allowing for reliable tracking. Temporal differences between frames yield actionable metrics like velocity and distance. The breakdown regime occurs when temporal resolution is insufficient or when occlusions disrupt continuity. Dualities emerge in how static features map to evolving behaviors, with failure modes including misidentification or loss of feature fidelity. These primitives form a foundation for probabilistic inference in GSI and state transition logic in GSE.
